clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Honduran male with prior tapeworm infection presented with subacute episodic vertigo, nausea, left-sided tinnitus, and hearing loss. Initial neurological examination was normal with dizziness on Hallpike maneuver without nystagmus, leading to a provisional diagnosis of left-sided Meniere's disease. Audiological evaluation confirmed significant bilateral low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss consistent with Meniere's disease. Brain MRI subsequently revealed a 3 mm postinflammatory calcification in the right parietal lobe, establishing the diagnosis of neurocysticercosis. The patient was managed with dietary and lifestyle modifications and oral steroids.
